text.p: Nordic cement and building materials group Scancem AB on Thursday posted profits before tax for the first nine months of the year of 947 million Swedish crowns ($142.8 million), up 21 percent from 783 million crowns a year ago.
The result included a gain of 361 million crowns from the sale of activites including the sale of Belgian assets in the second quarter, a statement from the company said.
For the full year, Scancem said it expected to record a result of at least 1.1 billion crowns. In 1995 pre-tax profits totalled 955 million crowns.
In the third quarter Scancem booked its best ever result of 457 million crowns, compared with 308 million crowns in the cooresponding year-ago quarter.
Scancem's largest shareholders are Norway's Aker ASA and Sweden's Skanska AB with 33 percent each.
"The net effect on Scancem's result from the company's which were taken over from Aker is now positive. The effect in the third quarter was about 100 million crowns," the statement said.
"Scancem is expecting continued positive developments in its results for the rest of the year and expects a result for the whole of 1996 of at least 1.1 billion crowns."

Scancem said its business areas continued to be characterised by a relatively weak construction market in Sweden and Finland and positive developments in Norway and in Denmark. The international markets were mainly on the same level as last year, it said.
Earnings per share (EPS) in the first nine months amounted to 14.50 crowns versus 12.50 crowns. For the year the company forecast EPS at 17 crowns.
